questions.question: Factorising is best described as:
options: The reverse of expanding — recovering the brackets whose product is the expression

questions.question: For $x^2 + 6x + 8$, the two numbers needed have:
options: Product 8 and sum 6 — the numbers 2 and 4

questions.question: Before factorising any trinomial, the FIRST check is always:
options: Is there a common factor in all the terms?

subtopics.title: Verification, Sign Patterns and the Full Method

questions.question: The reliable way to verify a factorisation is:
options: Check that the brackets look symmetrical
Repeat the split with different numbers
Expand the brackets and confirm the original trinomial returns

questions.question: Target product positive and target sum negative means the two numbers are:
No factor pair of the target product gives the target sum. What does this mean?
options: The common factor was too big
The trinomial does not factorise over the integers — stating that is the answer
You must invent a pair that nearly works

questions.question: Factorising trinomials is the tool for how many terms?
options: Three terms — two-term expressions use squares/cubes identities, four-term ones use grouping

subtopics.title: Two Numbers That Multiply and Add

questions.question: To factorise $x^2 + 6x + 8$, the two numbers you hunt must:
options: Multiply to 8 and add to 6 — the numbers 2 and 4

questions.question: When $(x + 2)(x + 4)$ is expanded, the middle term $6x$ comes from:
options: Adding the two middle products $4x$ and $2x$

questions.question: For $3x^2 + 18x + 24$, the very first move is:
options: Taking out the common factor 3, leaving $3(x^2 + 6x + 8)$

subtopics.title: When the Number in Front Is Not a One

questions.question: For $6x^2 - 7x - 3$, the multiply-target is:
options: The front number times the last number: $6 \times (-3) = -18$

questions.question: A negative multiply-target together with a negative add-target means the pair is:
options: One positive and one negative, with the bigger one carrying the minus

questions.question: Which factor pair of 18 has a difference of 7?
Why does the pair $-9$ and $+2$ pass the check?
options: Because $-9 \times 2 = -18$ and $-9 + 2 = -7$ — both targets are met

questions.question: The check that proves $(2x - 3)(3x + 1)$ is correct is:
options: That both brackets contain an x
Multiplying the brackets out and getting $6x^2 - 7x - 3$ back
